title: I tried out OpenAI’s new AI keypad — which will be fun for some coders and slightly mystifying to everyone else
slides: Can a keypad make you a better coder?
OpenAI's new tool replaces typing with AI shortcuts.
It works like magic for Python, but not for prose.
Non-coders will stare at a blank, silent keyboard.
Try it yourself if you write code daily.
thread_text:
1. Become a coder overnight.

OpenAI built a keypad that completes code for you. It's not a theory—it's live today.

2. Python loves it.

For Python scripts, the tool predicts your next move. Prose? It stalls. The AI only helps with logic, not creativity.

3. Non-coders get silence.

If you don't code, the keyboard stays blank. No suggestions, no help—just a dark slab staring back.

4. The shortcut illusion.

Typing less seems like a win, but deleted AI lines add time. You trade keystrokes for mental overhead.

5. Test it on your own code.

Open the tool and run a Python function. Does it write cleaner than you? Try it once this week.

It works with Python, not with prose.

Try it if you write code daily.

instagram.caption:
OpenAI’s new keypad autocompletes your code, but if you don't write Python, the screen stays blank. No suggestions, no help—just silence.

Coders get lightning-fast Python predictions; writers get a dead keyboard. 🐍 The tool only assists logic, not creativity. Deleting wrong AI suggestions can even slow you down. ⏳

If you publish code daily, your typing is about to change. If you write anything else, this tool doesn't exist for you.

Run one Python function into it this week—did the shortcut actually save you time? 🤔
